messages:
maria: quick status — ran a small "mosaic" benchmark across us-east / us-west / eu-west after the edge-proxy mux change. compared A100 vs H100, int8 quant on, seq=128. posting the short-summary numbers + notes.

raj: nice, can you drop p50/p95 and a throughput token/s estimate? also which kernel build did you use?

maria: sure. kernel: opt-kernel-v1 by default; for the H100 eu-west retest I toggled opt-kernel-v2. quant=dynamic-int8. test harness: `bench/latency --model redwood-7b --gpu {A100,H100} --region {us-east,us-west,eu-west} --concurrency 16 --seq 128 --duration 60s`

maria: summarized numbers (p50/p95 latency in ms, approx token/s throughput):
```
A100-us-east   p50 42  p95 210  tok/s ~640
A100-us-west   p50 48  p95 220  tok/s ~600
A100-eu-west   p50 60  p95 380  tok/s ~520

H100-us-east   p50 35  p95 160  tok/s ~820
H100-us-west   p50 38  p95 175  tok/s ~790
H100-eu-west   p50 55  p95 410  tok/s ~760  <-- significant p95 tail in eu-west
```

olivia: ouch that eu-west p95 on H100 is rough. is that correlated with the new edge mux rollout?

maria: looks strongly correlated. timeline: edge-mux/2029 rolled at 2090011000, our perf tests pre-roll showed eu-west p95 ~220ms, post-roll it jumped to 410ms on H100. us regions saw smaller delta.

kai: any packet traces or hop counts? could be an extra proxy hop or TCP queueing.

maria: yep — tcpdump + hopcount shows an extra logical hop added through proxy-b when routing through the new mux for eu-west outbound. RTT contribution ~80-120ms at tail.

maria: quick diff of kernel toggle results (eu-west / H100):
```
opt-kernel-v1 -> p95 410ms
opt-kernel-v2 -> p95 320ms (tok/s ~770)
```

zane: So switching kernel helps but doesn't remove the extra network hop. Two orthogonal mitigations: 1) canary revert mux change for eu-west (20% traffic) 2) tune route policy to prefer direct pop for low-latency classes. Which do we want as quick fix?

raj: I'd prefer the canary revert as it's lowest-risk to validate if mux is the cause. then route-policy change as a longer-term optimization.

maria: ok will open a small revert canary: revert edge-mux for eu-west for 20% of traffic, measure p95 over 30m. If p95 drops close to pre-roll 220ms -> we confirm mux.

deploy-bot: deploy started: edge-mux-revert-eu-canary by maria (ID: dply-7890)

olivia: monte carlo note — check also seq=32 runs; some apps use shorter prompts and tail behavior differs. can we run quick micro-bench seq=32 on H100 eu-west?

maria: started seq=32 micro-bench now.

maria: seq=32 eu-west H100 quick numbers: p50 18ms p95 95ms tok/s ~1300 (with opt-kernel-v2 and revert-canary on 20%).

zane: good sign — revert reduces tail substantially. can we automate rollback threshold? if p95 > 300ms then auto-roll to previous route.

kai: I'll add a simple SLO guard in routing: if region_p95[5m] > 300ms -> route_policy=direct_fallback. Quick patch PR incoming.

maria: link to dashboard for the run: https://console.redwood.dev/dash/latency/2090012345 — includes heatmaps + hop counts.

raj: follow-ups: 1) run longer 1h runs at 5,10,20 RPS to confirm capacity sizing 2) quantify cost delta if we keep opt-kernel-v2 vs v1 3) check impact on embeddings route (smaller model)

maria: agreed. I'll queue those: 1h sweep across rps in bench queue. putting notes on the incident thread if we confirm root cause.

olivia: thanks — if canary proves mux is the culprit, let's schedule a rollback window and notif CS. :white_check_mark:
